prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1490; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound on a two-lane road in Conroe, Texas, when the vehicle struck the front of a northbound sedan operated by Driver 2. The impact was low speed, but the front bumper, hood and both headlight assemblies show damage that is generally consistent with a head-on contact of this kind. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain at the scene and was transported for evaluation. A passenger in the vehicle was also present, though the responding officer could not fully determine the seating position of the reporting driver at the moment of impact, as accounts differed slightly on that point. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 described it, and two independent witnesses gave consistent accounts. Scene photographs were taken and reviewed. No prior damage to either vehicle was noted by the responding officer. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
